title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic media failure rather than a model error. An AI system was used to alter a photograph of real, identifiable students, and the altered image was published on campus banners by a university dining unit. The edit did not add a caption or a label, so the fabricated depiction of the students was presented as a documentary photograph of an event that did not happen that way.

The failure occurred at the point of publication, not at the point of generation. Stanford's own AI policy prohibits using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, facilities or achievements, and requires disclosure. Catching it would have taken a review step that compared the banner image against the original photograph, and a disclosure that the image had been generated or edited. Both were available and neither happened.

What is not established is intent. Whether the alteration was deliberate, and who specifically made or approved it, is not stated in the reporting, and the finding that the policy was violated rests on the university's own account rather than on an outside determination.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior at Stanford majoring in human biology, was in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. Stanford's dining service posted the picture online the next day. When Stanford later used the image on campus banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the two other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to alter the original photo. The university said its AI policy strictly bans using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
